name: list_workspaces
description: List the workspaces you can reach (id, name, deviceId, deviceLabel, accessRole). A workspace with "unavailable" set is one its device no longer serves: sessions cannot start there until the person adds the folder again. A session token reaches every workspace of the person who started it, as at most Member; start work in another one only when the user asks for it.

name: list_resources
description: List what each device you can reach offers sessions (installed browsers, macOS screen control), whether it is online, and the workspaces on it where you may start a session. To use a resource on another device, start a session in one of that device's workspaces (create_session with workspaceId). Resources are the device's own software; nothing is installed for you.

name: list_profiles
description: List the agent profiles you can dispatch to (id, runtime, model, status) on one device: yours by default, or another device hosting a workspace you reach (see list_workspaces).

deviceId.description: Device that owns the profiles; defaults to the calling device.

name: list_models
description: List the models a profile can run (its endpoint's catalog), on your device by default or another device hosting a workspace you reach.

deviceId.description: Device that owns the profiles; defaults to the calling device.

name: create_session
description: Create a new Foundry session and deliver it a task. With a session token the new session is your child; in your own workspace (the default) it runs on your device, joins your orchestration group and, without profileId and provider, runs like you. Name workspaceId to start it in another workspace you reach (list_workspaces), on that workspace's device, only when the user asked for work there. Returns once queued unless wait=true, which blocks until it settles and returns its response. Parallel sessions writing the same repository race: split independent work and keep one writer per target. To continue an existing session use send_message instead of creating a new one.

prompt.description: The task brief for the new session.

importedContext.description: Background the new session should know before the prompt.

verification.description: Run a read-only independent verifier (no Write/Edit/Bash); use for checking another session's work.

forkSessionId.description: Fork: resume another session's native transcript in a brand new thread.

issueId.description: Run inside that Issue's candidate worktree and sandbox (requires an active Issue run).

wait.description: Block until the session settles and return its response.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to start the session in; defaults to yours with a session token, required without one.

name: handoff_session
description: Start a fresh session that continues another one from facts only: its original goal, last recorded result and status, plus your prompt. Use it instead of fork when the old transcript is misleading or too long.

prompt.description: What the new session should do next.

name: list_sessions
description: List sessions in a workspace (id, title, status, parentSessionId): yours by default. Use it to see what exists before creating or acting.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to list; defaults to yours with a session token.

name: list_group_sessions
description: List every session in one orchestration group, in list order. A replacement orchestrator uses this to take over a group without lineage transfer.

name: get_session
description: Get a compact summary of any session or synced native chat you can read, in any workspace you reach: title, status and error, runtime/profile/model, device (and whether it is online), workspace, times, lineage, event counts, the last answer (first 1000 characters), the last error event with the events just before it, and background tasks still open in its latest turn. Read events with read_context scope=events.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link (https://<host>/chats/<id>?workspace=…).

name: read_context
description: Read a session or native chat you can read, in any workspace you reach, by id or Foundry link. scope=summary (default) is get_session's summary; events lists its events one line each (time | level | label | detail), filtered by levels, labels and query, newest with tail or paged with after/before cursors, within maxBytes; thread (the session's full transcript), transcript (raw native chat) and subagents (the session's native subagents; with taskId, one subagent's transcript) return JSON cut at maxBytes. Start with summary and events; read thread or transcript only when you need the whole conversation.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link (https://<host>/chats/<id>?workspace=…).

levels.description: scope=events: only events of these levels, e.g. ["error","warning"].

labels.description: scope=events: only events with these labels (exact, case-insensitive), e.g. ["Session failed"].

query.description: scope=events: only events whose label, detail or message contains this text (case-insensitive).

tail.description: scope=events: the last N matching events (at most 500). Without it, the first `limit` matches.

limit.description: scope=events: page size without tail; default 50, at most 500.

after.description: scope=events: only events after this cursor, an event id this tool printed or a time (2026-10-09T20:40:00Z).

before.description: scope=events: only events before this cursor, an event id or a time.

context.description: scope=events: also show up to N events (at most 5) just before each match, to see what led to it.

taskId.description: With scope=subagents: the subagent to read.

maxBytes.description: Default 12000. events keeps whole lines within it and prints the cursor that continues.

name: send_message
description: Send a message to any session in this workspace. A running session is steered (Claude adjusts its active turn; Codex queues it for the next one). An idle session takes it as its next input and continues the same native session; profileId/provider/model switch its runtime first. wait=true blocks until it settles and returns its response.

wait.description: Block until the session settles and return its response.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

name: cancel_session
description: Stop the work a session in this workspace is doing. Cancelling never cascades: sessions it created keep running. The session stays usable: send_message continues it.

name: wait_session
description: Block until a session reaches one of the requested statuses (default: completed/failed/canceled) or the timeout elapses, and return it with its response once settled. Prefer this over polling loops.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

name: rename_session
description: Rename a session in this workspace (1-120 characters).

name: ask_person
description: Only for the execution of an Issue: ask the person something only they can decide (a choice the confirmed contract leaves open) or allow (a side effect outside the candidate, such as deploying or sending a message). After calling it, end your turn with a short summary of where you are; the Issue waits for the person and Foundry resumes you in the same candidate with their answer. Ask one question at a time and never about anything you can decide yourself.

question.description: What you need, in the person's language, with the context they need to answer.

kind.description: input: a decision or information; permission: approval for a specific action. Defaults to input.

options.description: Up to 6 suggested answers; the person may answer otherwise.
